content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-inference::inference-serving region=us-west-2 az=az3 — elevated 5xx rate and sustained KV cache evictions (threshold breach). PD: P0

pagerduty: Page triggered to schedule: oncall-sre-us-west-2 (Alex Kim) — urgency: high

Alex Kim: acked — investigating. seeing spike in errors, routing fallback not yet active. tagging @Priya @Ben

Priya Rao: joining. quick ask — any customers reported errors? Julia from CS looped?

Julia (CS): received 3 support tickets mentioning timeouts for embedding runs in us-west-2. Customer A on dedicated pool reports increased tail latency. I'll surface more details.

Ben Thomas: looking at telemetry — RL shard eviction counts jumping, node OOMs intermittently, autoscaler pulling nodes but some go into NotReady. suspecting NIC flaps after vm agent updates.

Sasha Ng: thanks. can we confirm whether routing fallback to az2 is enabled? last config push toggled fallback window to 15m.

Morgan (oncall-sre): I see the `routing.fallback.window` still 15m. not yet triggered because capacity in other AZs was borderline. recommend manual activation of fallback to preserve customer traffic.

Alex Kim: agreed. manual activate fallback to route user traffic away from az3 to az2/az4 for inference-serving. Priya, can you run the rollout?

Priya Rao: initiating manual fallback. command: ```/ops fallback activate --service inference-serving --from az3 --to az2,az4 --percent 100 --reason "az3 KV eviction surge"```

ops-bot: Received command from Priya Rao. Starting routing policy change. Will drain new requests from az3 and divert to az2/az4. Estimated propagation: ~45s.

Ben Thomas: while fallback propagates, I'm collecting pod logs and kernel OOM lines. sample from node-az3-7:`
```
[2026-03-15T21:12:08Z] eviction: reclaiming memory, killed process python(4823)
[2026-03-15T21:12:09Z] net: device eth0 link is down
[2026-03-15T21:12:10Z] kubelet evicting pods due to memory pressure
```

Sasha Ng: that link down line is consistent with NIC driver churn post-update. ops-infra, any rolling kernel/agent updates in az3 last hour?

Alex Kim: ops-infra confirms a staged NIC driver rollout started ~20m ago. they paused after anomalies but some hosts remained in the pool. I'll ask them to halt and start remediation.

ops-bot: Routing fallback is 95% propagated. Traffic to az3 reduced to ~8% of baseline. Error rate trending down from 5xx: 12% -> 2.1% over 90s.

Priya Rao: enabling autoscaler backoff to avoid oscillation in az3 while infra remediation completes: ```/ops autoscaler set-backoff --pool az3 --duration 30m --reason "prevent thrash"```

Morgan (oncall-sre): captured heap profile and KV cache metrics for postmortem. saving to s3://redwood-incidents/6734567891/ for later.

Julia (CS): updating impacted customers: sending templated note — outage in us-west-2/az3 affecting some inference requests; traffic being diverted; expected mitigation in 30-60m. Will update as we learn more.

Ben Thomas: ops-infra will revert NIC driver on hosts that failed health checks. estimated host remediation per batch ~12m.

Alex Kim: good. next steps: (1) monitor error rate and latency while fallback holds, (2) ops-infra to remediate drivers in az3, (3) do controlled reintroduce of az3 after 2 successive 10m healthy windows, (4) post-incident follow-up with rollback plan. tagging @SRE-leads for postmortem.

pagerduty: Alert status: acknowledged by Alex Kim. Escalation paused.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-az3-kv-evictions. Severity: P0. Runbook link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-20260315-az3-kv-evictions

Alex Kim: thanks team. handing to Morgan for steady-state monitoring. I'm going offline for 25m but reachable if needed.

Morgan (oncall-sre): taking handoff. will post updates every 10m or on significant change. current status: fallback active, customer impact reduced, infra remediation in progress.

Julia (CS): will keep CS/AE on a 30m cadence. posting update to Customer A now.

Sasha Ng: logging action items for postmortem: confirm canary/rollout tool prevented full rollout, why some hosts remained, why autoscaler didn't detect NIC flaps sooner, and add healthcheck for driver-change in az.

Alex Kim: closing note — great coordination. once we have stable metrics for 30m, we'll consider closing PD but keep incident open for postmortem.

Morgan (oncall-sre): update @channel — 30m check-in: errors steady at 0.8%, tail latency back to baseline, infra remediation progressing. will update again at 22:15 UTC.
